addedLines: - build-log-checker: Scan a Buildroot build log for failures and report which package broke, on which target. Use after a build run in the mx_SNMP_PLAN_E container when the log needs triage. Read-only — it never edits files or starts a build. (Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- adr: Record and enforce Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in Markdown under ~/mds4xgl3/.adr/. Use when creating or updating an ADR, when the user mentions ADR / architecture decision / .adr, or before making architectural or cross-module changes that could conflict with prior decisions.
- brainstorming: Turn an idea into an approved design spec through one-question-at-a-time dialogue, before any code is written. Use when the user invokes it explicitly, or asks to brainstorm, spec out, or design a feature or module up front.
- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- design-an-interface: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- dut-console: Drive the serial console at /dev/ttyS0 connected to the Moxa MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS DUT. Logs in as admin/moxa, su's to root (password moxa) if at a Linux shell, runs the provided commands, and writes all I/O to ~/console_<date>_<time>.log. Use when the user asks to run commands on the DUT, verify behavior on the physical device, check device state via console, or snmpwalk/snmpset against the connected hardware.
- examinate-plan-e-swu: Examine, upload and flash a Plan E .swu firmware image on the Moxa MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS DUT. Reports which dual-image partition the update will overwrite before touching anything, refuses to overwrite the mainline control group, scp's the .swu to /tmp, hard-gates on an md5 comparison, then runs swupdate + sync + reboot. Use when the user wants to check a .swu, put a new Plan E build on the device, verify a full image (not a hot-swapped binary), or asks which partition is about to be overwritten.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- git-guardrails-claude-code: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- migrate-to-shoehorn: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.
- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the Obsidian vault with wikilinks and index notes. Use when user wants to find, create, or organize notes in Obsidian.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- qa: Interactive QA session where user reports bugs or issues conversationally, and the agent files GitHub issues. Explores the codebase in the background for context and domain language. Use when user wants to report bugs, do QA, file issues conversationally, or mentions "QA session".
- request-refactor-plan: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- rust-clippy-by-application: Use when MXNOS/buildroot Rust clippy scan fails under a pinned rustc (e.g. rustc 1.85, "rustc 1.85.0 is not supported", icu_*/bytestring/actix needing 1.86/1.88) because packages re-resolve crates without a Cargo.lock; or when converting per-package clippy scanning to per-application; or rolling out the per-package GitLab issue+branch+MR changes across many dl repos.
- scaffold-exercises: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.
- session-to-doc: Turn a whole Claude Code session (reference material gathered, the discussion in the middle, and the final conclusions) into ONE structured Markdown document that doubles as (a) standalone explanatory documentation and (b) a slide-ready outline. Trigger on: "整理這次 session", "把這段對話 整理成文件", "session to doc", "做成投影片大綱", "summarize this session into a doc", or after a /export transcript is provided.
- setup-pre-commit: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

=== switch_ci_pipeline.yml ===
include:
  - local: utility/util_text_color.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/build.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/upload_artifact.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/bvt.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/actt.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/trigger_sqa_ci_pipeline.yml

variables:
  BR_DIR: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/moxabuild/buildroot
  BR_OUTPUT_DIR: $BR_DIR/output
  FWR_IMG_DIR: $BR_OUTPUT_DIR/images
  FWR_BUILD_DIR: $BR_OUTPUT_DIR/build
  FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE: $BR_DIR/build.log
  FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE: $BR_DIR/CHANGELOG.txt
  # Baseline config from last successful pipeline on the same branch.
  # This file will be fetched early to generate revision-based CHANGELOG.txt.
  BASELINE_CONFIG_FILE: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/baseline/FWR_baseline.config
  FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE: $FWR_IMG_DIR/PIPELINE_INFO.txt
  BD_PKG_DIR: $BR_DIR/classifications
  COVERITY_SW_PKGS: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/moxabuild/coverity/software-packages.yml
  # Force build firmware to ignore source code change checking.
  # Set to 'true' to initiate force build.
  FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "false"

workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $COVERITY_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_CONFIG == "true" && $COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG == "false"
      when: never
    # Only run pipeline when manual trigger (web) or schedule
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web"
      variables:
        FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "true"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api"
      variables:
        FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "true"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

default:
  tags:
    - autoscale-dev-ops
  retry:
    max: 1
    when:
      - runner_system_failure
  cache: &global_cache
    key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}
    paths:
      - $FWR_IMG_DIR/*
      - $FWR_BUILD_DIR/*.log
      - $FWR_BUILD_DIR/*.txt

stages:
  - build
  - upload
  - bvt
  - actt
  - trigger

build-code:
  extends: .build
  stage: build
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
    # The size of build log exceeds the limit if gitlab runner,
    # the alternative is to preserve as artifact along with the job.
    - $FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE
    - $FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE
    - $FWR_IMG_DIR/*.config
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  cache:
    - <<: *global_cache
      policy: push
    - key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}-bd-packages
      policy: push
      paths:
        - $BD_PKG_DIR

build-code:cov-build:
  extends: .cov-build
  stage: build
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - $FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE
      - $FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE
      - $COVERITY_SW_PKGS
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  rules:
    - if: $COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG !=  "false"
  cache: []

build-code:upload: # When changing job name, please also update the job name in build.yml:func_fetch_baseline_config
  extends: .upload_artifacts
  stage: upload
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - $FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      - baseline/FWR_baseline.config
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull-push

bvt:
  extends: .bvt
  stage: bvt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  # A gitlab project wise resource group to prevent concurrent BVT jobs
  # on the same testbed. Scoped by BVT_RUNNER_TAG so different product models
  # (wired to different runners/testbeds) can run BVT in parallel, while jobs
  # targeting the same runner are still serialized.
  resource_group: testbed_bvt_${BVT_RUNNER_TAG}
  rules:
    - if: $BVT ==  "true"

auto-test:actt:
  extends: .actt
  stage: actt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  # Project-wide resource group: only one ACTT job at a time (same ACTT Windows host / Docker testbed).
  # One product repo per model is expected to map to one testbed; adjust name if multiple ACTT hosts are introduced.
  resource_group: testbed_actt
  rules:
    - if: $ACTT == "true"
    # - if: '$ACTT == "true" && ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api")'

auto-test:actt_upload_report:
  extends: .actt_upload_report
  stage: actt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  needs:
    - job: auto-test:actt
      artifacts: true
  # No resource_group: does not SSH to ACTT testbed; uploads artifacts from actt via scm runner.
  rules:
    - if: $ACTT == "true"
    # - if: '$ACTT == "true" && ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api")'

trigger_bd_scan:
  stage: trigger
  trigger:
    include:
      - project: 'moxa/sw/switch/general/infra/ci/management/ci-pipeline'
        # Test branch: keep child pipelines on the same ref as this experiment.
        ref: main-autoscale-dev-ops
        file: 'pipeline_bd_scan/bd_scan_pipeline.yml'
  rules:
    - if: $BLACKDUCK_SCAN_CONFIG !=  "N/A"

trigger_rust_clippy_report:
  stage: trigger
  trigger:
    include:
      - project: 'moxa/sw/switch/general/infra/ci/management/ci-pipeline'
        # Test branch: keep child pipelines on the same ref as this experiment.
        ref: main-autoscale-dev-ops
        file: 'pipeline_rust_clippy_report/rust_clippy_report_pipeline.yml'
  rules:
    - if: $RUST_CLIPPY_SCAN_CONFIG ==  "true"

trigger_sqa_ci_pipeline:
  extends: .trigger_sqa_ci_autotest
  stage: trigger
  cache:
    - <<: *global_cache
      policy: pull
  rules:

include:
  - local: utility/util_text_color.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/build.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/upload_artifact.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/bvt.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/actt.yml
  - local: pipeline_main/trigger_sqa_ci_pipeline.yml

variables:
  BR_DIR: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/moxabuild/buildroot
  BR_OUTPUT_DIR: $BR_DIR/output
  FWR_IMG_DIR: $BR_OUTPUT_DIR/images
  FWR_BUILD_DIR: $BR_OUTPUT_DIR/build
  FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE: $BR_DIR/build.log
  FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE: $BR_DIR/CHANGELOG.txt
  # Baseline config from last successful pipeline on the same branch.
  # This file will be fetched early to generate revision-based CHANGELOG.txt.
  BASELINE_CONFIG_FILE: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/baseline/FWR_baseline.config
  FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE: $FWR_IMG_DIR/PIPELINE_INFO.txt
  BD_PKG_DIR: $BR_DIR/classifications
  COVERITY_SW_PKGS: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/moxabuild/coverity/software-packages.yml
  # Force build firmware to ignore source code change checking.
  # Set to 'true' to initiate force build.
  FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "false"

workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $COVERITY_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_CONFIG == "true" && $COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG == "false"
      when: never
    # Only run pipeline when manual trigger (web) or schedule
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web"
      variables:
        FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "true"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api"
      variables:
        FWR_FORCE_BUILD: "true"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

default:
  tags:
    - autoscale-dev-ops
  retry:
    max: 1
    when:
      - runner_system_failure
  cache: &global_cache
    key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}
    paths:
      - $FWR_IMG_DIR/*
      - $FWR_BUILD_DIR/*.log
      - $FWR_BUILD_DIR/*.txt

stages:
  - build
  - upload
  - bvt
  - actt
  - trigger

build-code:
  extends: .build
  stage: build
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
    # The size of build log exceeds the limit if gitlab runner,
    # the alternative is to preserve as artifact along with the job.
    - $FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE
    - $FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE
    - $FWR_IMG_DIR/*.config
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  cache:
    - <<: *global_cache
      policy: push
    - key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}-bd-packages
      policy: push
      paths:
        - $BD_PKG_DIR

build-code:cov-build:
  extends: .cov-build
  stage: build
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - $FWR_BUILD_LOG_FILE
      - $FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE
      - $COVERITY_SW_PKGS
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  rules:
    - if: $COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG !=  "false"
  cache: []

build-code:upload: # When changing job name, please also update the job name in build.yml:func_fetch_baseline_config
  extends: .upload_artifacts
  stage: upload
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - $FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      - baseline/FWR_baseline.config
    when: always
    expire_in: 30 days
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull-push

bvt:
  extends: .bvt
  stage: bvt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  # A gitlab project wise resource group to prevent concurrent BVT jobs
  # on the same testbed. Scoped by BVT_RUNNER_TAG so different product models
  # (wired to different runners/testbeds) can run BVT in parallel, while jobs
  # targeting the same runner are still serialized.
  resource_group: testbed_bvt_${BVT_RUNNER_TAG}
  rules:
    - if: $BVT ==  "true"

auto-test:actt:
  extends: .actt
  stage: actt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  # Project-wide resource group: only one ACTT job at a time (same ACTT Windows host / Docker testbed).
  # One product repo per model is expected to map to one testbed; adjust name if multiple ACTT hosts are introduced.
  resource_group: testbed_actt
  rules:
    - if: $ACTT == "true"
    # - if: '$ACTT == "true" && ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api")'

auto-test:actt_upload_report:
  extends: .actt_upload_report
  stage: actt
  allow_failure:
    exit_codes:
      - 3
  cache:
    <<: *global_cache
    policy: pull
  needs:
    - job: auto-test:actt
      artifacts: true
  # No resource_group: does not SSH to ACTT testbed; uploads artifacts from actt via scm runner.
  rules:
    - if: $ACTT == "true"
    # - if: '$ACTT == "true" && ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api")'

trigger_bd_scan:
  stage: trigger
  trigger:
    include:
      - project: 'moxa/sw/switch/general/infra/ci/management/ci-pipeline'
        # Test branch: keep child pipelines on the same ref as this experiment.
        ref: main-autoscale-dev-ops
        file: 'pipeline_bd_scan/bd_scan_pipeline.yml'
  rules:
    - if: $BLACKDUCK_SCAN_CONFIG !=  "N/A"

trigger_rust_clippy_report:
  stage: trigger
  trigger:
    include:
      - project: 'moxa/sw/switch/general/infra/ci/management/ci-pipeline'
        # Test branch: keep child pipelines on the same ref as this experiment.
        ref: main-autoscale-dev-ops
        file: 'pipeline_rust_clippy_report/rust_clippy_report_pipeline.yml'
  rules:
    - if: $RUST_CLIPPY_SCAN_CONFIG ==  "true"

trigger_sqa_ci_pipeline:
  extends: .trigger_sqa_ci_autotest
  stage: trigger
  cache:
    - <<: *global_cache
      policy: pull
  rules:
    - if: $SQA_CI_TEST_LEVEL !=  "N/A"

===== bvt.yml =====
.bvt:
  # Currently we use default docker image on the RDVM runner, no neeed to specify image here.
  # image: $SRE_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GITLAB_IMAGE_PREFIX/moxa/sw/sre/share/runner-img/docker-git:latest
  # Use RDVM runner instead of autoscale runner for safe SSH connection to testbed.
  # Runner tag from pipeline variables: default in autobuild_config_prefill_global_var.yml;
  # override in product autobuild_config.yml. Do not set BVT_RUNNER_TAG here — job variables
  # would override the product and force every project onto the same RDVM.
  tags:
    - $BVT_RUNNER_TAG
  variables:
    RUNNER_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT: 1h50m     # Leave 10 mins for after script operation
    RUNNER_AFTER_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT: 10m # Change after script timeout from 5m (default) to 10m
  before_script:
    # Skip this stage if FWR_FORCE_BUILD is false AND no new changes
    - |
      if [ "${FWR_FORCE_BUILD}" == "false" ] && [ ! -s "$FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No new changes today, skip BVT stage.${LOG_END}"
        exit 3
      fi
    # Get BVT parameters
    # Model name is case insensitive
    - BVT_FWR_URL=$(sed -n 's/^SCM_URL=//p' "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" | head -n 1)
    - BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL=$(echo "$BVT_FWR_URL" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
    # Export BVT parameters as environment variables for ssh command
    - export BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL=${BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL}
    - export BVT_FWR_URL=${BVT_FWR_URL}
  script:
    - |
      echo "${LOG_INFO}Start BVT${LOG_END}"
      echo "${LOG_INFO}BVT parameters:${LOG_END}"
      echo "Product model = ${BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL}"
      echo "SCM Firmware URL = ${BVT_FWR_URL}"
    - eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
    - chmod 600 "$BVT_TESTBED_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - ssh-add "$BVT_TESTBED_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no ${BVT_TESTBED_SSH_USERNAME}@${BVT_TESTBED_SSH_IP} "bash ./run_bvt.sh $BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL $BVT_FWR_URL" || exit_code=$?
    - |
      if [ "${exit_code}" -ne "0" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_ERR}BVT failed, please refer to test log for details. (exit_code=${exit_code})${LOG_END}"
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "${LOG_INFO}BVT succeed.${LOG_END}"
===== actt.yml =====
.actt:
  # Runner tag comes from pipeline variables (prefill default + optional product override). Same as `.bvt`.
  tags:
    - $BVT_RUNNER_TAG
  variables:
    ACTT_IMAGE_TAG: "latest"
    DUT_VERSION: "0.0.0"
    GIT_STRATEGY: none
    TEST_MARK: "actt"
    # DUT_MODEL must come from the product project's pipeline variables (e.g. autobuild_config.yml). Do not redefine it here — job-level variables would override the product and cause File API 404s.
    ALLURE_PROJECT_ID: $DUT_MODEL
    ACTT_IMAGE: "registry.gitlab.com/moxa/sw/sre/share/team-docker-images/maf/docker-actt/actt:${ACTT_IMAGE_TAG}"
    WIN_WORK_DIR: "C:/actt-run/$CI_JOB_ID"
    MAF_DEPLOY_USER: "gitlab+deploy-token-12868893"
    # Primary network at `docker run --network=...`. Second NIC: script runs `docker network connect ${DOCKER_NETWORK2}` — that network must exist on the ACTT Windows host (create once, admin PowerShell).
    DOCKER_NETWORK: "MyTransparentNetwork"
    # Host one-shot (fix typo: options are com.docker..., not om.docker). Backtick must be last char on each line; interface name must match Get-NetAdapter on that PC.
    #   docker network create -d transparent `
    #     --subnet=192.168.127.0/24 `
    #     -o com.docker.network.windowsshim.networkname="MyTransparentNetwork2" `
    #     -o com.docker.network.windowsshim.interface="Ethernet 2" `
    #     MyTransparentNetwork2
    DOCKER_NETWORK2: "MyTransparentNetwork2"
    ACTT_SSH_USERNAME: "moxa"
    # Repo-relative path is actt_config/<this filename> ($DUT_MODEL from product pipeline variables).
    DUT_ACTT_CONFIG: "${DUT_MODEL}.yaml"
    DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST: "dut_config"
    # GitLab Files API path segment; before_script re-exports DUT_ACTT_CONFIG / ACTT_CFG_REL using the same DUT_MODEL.
    ACTT_CFG_REL: "actt_config/$DUT_ACTT_CONFIG"
    # Filled from PIPELINE_INFO (same SCM_URL as BVT); optional override via CI/CD variables.
    SCM_FILE_PATH: ""
    ALLURE_SERVER: "10.123.25.160"
  before_script:
    # Skip this stage if FWR_FORCE_BUILD is false AND no new changes
    - |
      if [ "${FWR_FORCE_BUILD}" == "false" ] && [ ! -s "$FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No new changes today, skip ACTT stage.${LOG_END}"
        exit 3
      fi
    # Resolve DUT_MODEL / DUT_VERSION / SCM_FILE_PATH from upload stage (same source as bvt.yml).
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -z "${DUT_MODEL}" ] || [ "${DUT_MODEL}" = "NO_DEFAULT_DUT_MODEL" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: DUT_MODEL is unset or still NO_DEFAULT_DUT_MODEL. Define it under variables: in your product autobuild_config.yml (same as other switch products)."
        exit 1
      fi
      if [ -z "${SCM_FILE_PATH}" ]; then
        if [ ! -s "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ]; then
          echo "ERROR: ${FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE} missing or empty; run upload stage and ensure cache restores images dir."
          exit 1
        fi
        SCM_FILE_PATH=$(sed -n 's/^SCM_URL=//p' "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" | head -n 1)
      fi
      SCM_FILE_PATH=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed 's#/\([[:space:]]*\)#/#g')
      export SCM_FILE_PATH
      DUT_SERIES=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
      export DUT_SERIES
      export DUT_MODEL
      # FWR_<model>_v7.0_2026_... → 7.0 (stop at first _ after _v)
      DUT_VERSION=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed -n 's#.*/[Ff][Ww][Rr]_[^_]*_v\([^_]*\).*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
      export DUT_VERSION
      export DUT_ACTT_CONFIG="${DUT_MODEL}.yaml"
      export ACTT_CFG_REL="actt_config/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}"
      export ALLURE_PROJECT_ID="${DUT_MODEL}"
      echo "ACTT firmware context: DUT_MODEL=${DUT_MODEL} DUT_VERSION=${DUT_VERSION} DUT_SERIES=${DUT_SERIES}"
      echo "SCM_FILE_PATH=${SCM_FILE_PATH}"
      echo "ACTT_IMAGE=${ACTT_IMAGE}"
    - mkdir -p ~/.ssh && echo "StrictHostKeyChecking no" > ~/.ssh/config
    - chmod 600 "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
    - ssh-add "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    # - ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"hostname; whoami\""
  script:
    # Create remote working directory on Windows host
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report'"
    # Dump all CI variables to env file (exclude SSH secrets)
    - printenv | grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*=' | grep -vE '^(ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY|PATH)=' > /tmp/ci.env
    # Download project-dependent configuration file (GIT_STRATEGY: none — fetch via API, then scp to testbed)
    - |
      ACTT_CFG_ENC=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse,sys; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1], safe=''))" "$ACTT_CFG_REL")
      curl -fsS --header "JOB-TOKEN:${CI_JOB_TOKEN}" "${CI_API_V4_URL}/projects/${CI_PROJECT_ID}/repository/files/${ACTT_CFG_ENC}/raw?ref=${CI_COMMIT_SHA}" -o "/tmp/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}"
      echo "Windows work directory = ${WIN_WORK_DIR}"
      ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}'"
      scp "/tmp/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}" ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}
      echo "Verifying ${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG} under ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST} ..."
      ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"\$p='${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}'; if (Test-Path -LiteralPath \$p) { Write-Host ('CONFIRMED: ' + (Split-Path -Leaf \$p) + ' exists at ' + \$p); Get-Item -LiteralPath \$p | Format-List Name,Length,FullName } else { Write-Error ('MISSING: ' + \$p); exit 1 }\""
    # Generate per-job Docker auth config on runner to avoid Windows Credential Manager issues via SSH
    - mkdir -p /tmp/.docker
    - AUTH=$(printf "%s:%s" "${CI_REGISTRY_USER}" "${CI_JOB_TOKEN}" | base64 | tr -d '\n') && printf '{"auths":{"%s":{"auth":"%s"}}}' "${CI_REGISTRY}" "${AUTH}" > /tmp/.docker/config.json
    # Generate PowerShell test script (heredoc avoids cross-platform escaping issues)
    # Variables are NOT expanded here; they are injected into the container via --env-file
    - |
      cat << 'PSEOF' > /tmp/run_test.ps1
      Set-Location /app/test
      python ./tool/download_firmware.py $env:DUT_MODEL
      python initialize.py -t -m $env:DUT_MODEL -v $env:DUT_VERSION -tm $env:TEST_MARK -r $env:ALLURE_SERVER
      if (Test-Path "/app/test/report/allure") { Remove-Item -Path "/app/test/report/allure" -Recurse -Force }
      Copy-Item -Path "/app/test/report/*" -Destination "C:/CI_Out_Report/" -Recurse -Force
      Copy-Item -Path "/app/bin/log/application.log" -Destination "C:/CI_Out_Report/" -Force
      PSEOF
    - |
      cat << PSEOF > /tmp/run_actt_container.ps1
      docker --config ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker run -d \`
        --name ${CI_JOB_ID} \`
        --network=${DOCKER_NETWORK} \`
        --env-file ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/ci.env \`
        -v ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report:C:/CI_Out_Report \`
        -v ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}:C:/app/test/environment/dut \`
        ${ACTT_IMAGE} powershell -Command 'Start-Sleep 3600'
      if (\$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Error 'Failed to start container'; exit 1 }
      docker network connect ${DOCKER_NETWORK2} ${CI_JOB_ID}
      docker exec ${CI_JOB_ID} powershell -File C:\CI_Out_Report\run_test.ps1
      \$exitCode = \$LASTEXITCODE
      docker stop ${CI_JOB_ID} | Out-Null
      docker rm ${CI_JOB_ID} | Out-Null
      exit \$exitCode
      PSEOF
    # Copy env file, test script, and Docker auth config to Windows host
    - scp /tmp/ci.env /tmp/run_test.ps1 /tmp/run_actt_container.ps1 ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/
    - scp -r /tmp/.docker ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker
    # DEBUG: verify Docker config (cmd has no `cat`; do not print full config.json — contains registry auth / job token material)
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker' -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Format-Table Name,Length -AutoSize\""
    # Pull ACTT image on Windows host using per-job Docker config (isolated credentials, safe for concurrent pipelines)
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "docker --config ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker pull ${ACTT_IMAGE}"
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_actt_container.ps1
    # Remove helper files before pulling report to avoid leaking CI variables into artifacts
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command Remove-Item -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/ci.env','${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_test.ps1' ,'${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_actt_container.ps1' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue"
    # Pull report back from Windows host to runner workspace
    - scp -r ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report ./report
  after_script:
    # after_script runs in a new shell; ssh-agent is gone, use -i to specify key file directly
    - ssh -i "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY" -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}" "powershell -NoProfile -Command Remove-Item -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue" || true
    - ssh -i "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY" -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}" "docker image prune -f" || true
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - report/

.actt_upload_report:
  image: registry.gitlab.com/moxa/sw/sre/share/runner-img/docker-scm:latest
  variables:
    # Inherited from product autobuild_config.yml (pipeline variables); must not duplicate DUT_MODEL here or it overrides the product.
    # scm upload: --scm-path = SCM repo path; third arg = destination under repo → .../${DUT_MODEL}/report/${TEST_DATE}/
    ACTT_MAF_TARGET: "moxa/sw/sre/share/team-docker-images/maf/docker-actt"
  before_script:
    # Skip when the upstream actt job produced no report (e.g. it was skipped).
    - |
      if [ ! -d "report" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A report 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No ACTT report found, skip report upload.${LOG_END}"
        exit 3
      fi
  script:
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -z "${DUT_MODEL}" ] || [ "${DUT_MODEL}" = "NO_DEFAULT_DUT_MODEL" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: DUT_MODEL required for report upload path. Set it under variables: in autobuild_config.yml."
        exit 1
      fi
      if [ -n "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ] && [ -s "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ]; then
        _SCM=$(sed -n 's/^SCM_URL=//p' "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" | head -n 1)
        _SCM=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed 's#/\([[:space:]]*\)#/#g')
        export DUT_SERIES=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
        _VER=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed -n 's#.*/[Ff][Ww][Rr]_[^_]*_v\([^_]*\).*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
        export DUT_VERSION="$_VER"
        echo "actt_upload_report: DUT_MODEL=${DUT_MODEL} DUT_VERSION=${DUT_VERSION} DUT_SERIES=${DUT_SERIES}"
      fi
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -f report/result_summary.json ]; then
        TEST_DATE=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('report/result_summary.json'))['date'])")
      else
        echo "WARN: report/result_summary.json missing; using CI_PIPELINE_CREATED_AT for SCM path segment"
        TEST_DATE=$(date -d "$CI_PIPELINE_CREATED_AT" +"%Y-%m-%d-%H")
      fi
      echo "TEST_DATE=${TEST_DATE}"
      echo "Upload report/ → ${ACTT_MAF_TARGET}/${DUT_MODEL}/report/${TEST_DATE}/"
      scm upload --local-path report/ --scm-path "${ACTT_MAF_TARGET}" "report/${DUT_MODEL}/${TEST_DATE}"

    - BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL=$(echo "$BVT_FWR_URL" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)

    - export BVT_FWR_URL=${BVT_FWR_URL}
  script:
    - |
      echo "${LOG_INFO}Start BVT${LOG_END}"
      echo "${LOG_INFO}BVT parameters:${LOG_END}"
      echo "Product model = ${BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL}"
      echo "SCM Firmware URL = ${BVT_FWR_URL}"
    - eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
    - chmod 600 "$BVT_TESTBED_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - ssh-add "$BVT_TESTBED_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no ${BVT_TESTBED_SSH_USERNAME}@${BVT_TESTBED_SSH_IP} "bash ./run_bvt.sh $BVT_PRODUCT_MODEL $BVT_FWR_URL" || exit_code=$?
    - |
      if [ "${exit_code}" -ne "0" ]; then

.actt:
  # Runner tag comes from pipeline variables (prefill default + optional product override). Same as `.bvt`.
  tags:
    - $BVT_RUNNER_TAG
  variables:
    ACTT_IMAGE_TAG: "latest"
    DUT_VERSION: "0.0.0"
    GIT_STRATEGY: none
    TEST_MARK: "actt"
    # DUT_MODEL must come from the product project's pipeline variables (e.g. autobuild_config.yml). Do not redefine it here — job-level variables would override the product and cause File API 404s.
    ALLURE_PROJECT_ID: $DUT_MODEL
    ACTT_IMAGE: "registry.gitlab.com/moxa/sw/sre/share/team-docker-images/maf/docker-actt/actt:${ACTT_IMAGE_TAG}"
    WIN_WORK_DIR: "C:/actt-run/$CI_JOB_ID"
    MAF_DEPLOY_USER: "gitlab+deploy-token-12868893"
    # Primary network at `docker run --network=...`. Second NIC: script runs `docker network connect ${DOCKER_NETWORK2}` — that network must exist on the ACTT Windows host (create once, admin PowerShell).
    DOCKER_NETWORK: "MyTransparentNetwork"

    ACTT_SSH_USERNAME: "moxa"

    ACTT_CFG_REL: "actt_config/$DUT_ACTT_CONFIG"
    # Filled from PIPELINE_INFO (same SCM_URL as BVT); optional override via CI/CD variables.
    SCM_FILE_PATH: ""
    ALLURE_SERVER: "10.123.25.160"
  before_script:
    # Skip this stage if FWR_FORCE_BUILD is false AND no new changes
    - |
      if [ "${FWR_FORCE_BUILD}" == "false" ] && [ ! -s "$FWR_CHANGE_LOG_FILE" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No new changes today, skip ACTT stage.${LOG_END}"
        exit 3
      fi
    # Resolve DUT_MODEL / DUT_VERSION / SCM_FILE_PATH from upload stage (same source as bvt.yml).
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -z "${DUT_MODEL}" ] || [ "${DUT_MODEL}" = "NO_DEFAULT_DUT_MODEL" ]; then

        exit 1
      fi
      if [ -z "${SCM_FILE_PATH}" ]; then
        if [ ! -s "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ]; then
          echo "ERROR: ${FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE} missing or empty; run upload stage and ensure cache restores images dir."
          exit 1
        fi
        SCM_FILE_PATH=$(sed -n 's/^SCM_URL=//p' "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" | head -n 1)
      fi
      SCM_FILE_PATH=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed 's#/\([[:space:]]*\)#/#g')
      export SCM_FILE_PATH
      DUT_SERIES=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
      export DUT_SERIES
      export DUT_MODEL
      # FWR_<model>_v7.0_2026_... → 7.0 (stop at first _ after _v)
      DUT_VERSION=$(echo "$SCM_FILE_PATH" | sed -n 's#.*/[Ff][Ww][Rr]_[^_]*_v\([^_]*\).*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
      export DUT_VERSION
      export DUT_ACTT_CONFIG="${DUT_MODEL}.yaml"
      export ACTT_CFG_REL="actt_config/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}"
      export ALLURE_PROJECT_ID="${DUT_MODEL}"
      echo "ACTT firmware context: DUT_MODEL=${DUT_MODEL} DUT_VERSION=${DUT_VERSION} DUT_SERIES=${DUT_SERIES}"
      echo "SCM_FILE_PATH=${SCM_FILE_PATH}"
      echo "ACTT_IMAGE=${ACTT_IMAGE}"
    - mkdir -p ~/.ssh && echo "StrictHostKeyChecking no" > ~/.ssh/config
    - chmod 600 "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    - eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
    - ssh-add "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"
    # - ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"hostname; whoami\""
  script:
    # Create remote working directory on Windows host
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report'"
    # Dump all CI variables to env file (exclude SSH secrets)
    - printenv | grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*=' | grep -vE '^(ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY|PATH)=' > /tmp/ci.env
    # Download project-dependent configuration file (GIT_STRATEGY: none — fetch via API, then scp to testbed)
    - |
      ACTT_CFG_ENC=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse,sys; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1], safe=''))" "$ACTT_CFG_REL")
      curl -fsS --header "JOB-TOKEN:${CI_JOB_TOKEN}" "${CI_API_V4_URL}/projects/${CI_PROJECT_ID}/repository/files/${ACTT_CFG_ENC}/raw?ref=${CI_COMMIT_SHA}" -o "/tmp/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}"
      echo "Windows work directory = ${WIN_WORK_DIR}"
      ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}'"
      scp "/tmp/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}" ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}
      echo "Verifying ${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG} under ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST} ..."
      ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"\$p='${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG}'; if (Test-Path -LiteralPath \$p) { Write-Host ('CONFIRMED: ' + (Split-Path -Leaf \$p) + ' exists at ' + \$p); Get-Item -LiteralPath \$p | Format-List Name,Length,FullName } else { Write-Error ('MISSING: ' + \$p); exit 1 }\""
    # Generate per-job Docker auth config on runner to avoid Windows Credential Manager issues via SSH
    - mkdir -p /tmp/.docker
    - AUTH=$(printf "%s:%s" "${CI_REGISTRY_USER}" "${CI_JOB_TOKEN}" | base64 | tr -d '\n') && printf '{"auths":{"%s":{"auth":"%s"}}}' "${CI_REGISTRY}" "${AUTH}" > /tmp/.docker/config.json
    # Generate PowerShell test script (heredoc avoids cross-platform escaping issues)
    # Variables are NOT expanded here; they are injected into the container via --env-file
    - |
      cat << 'PSEOF' > /tmp/run_test.ps1
      Set-Location /app/test
      python ./tool/download_firmware.py $env:DUT_MODEL
      python initialize.py -t -m $env:DUT_MODEL -v $env:DUT_VERSION -tm $env:TEST_MARK -r $env:ALLURE_SERVER
      if (Test-Path "/app/test/report/allure") { Remove-Item -Path "/app/test/report/allure" -Recurse -Force }
      Copy-Item -Path "/app/test/report/*" -Destination "C:/CI_Out_Report/" -Recurse -Force
      Copy-Item -Path "/app/bin/log/application.log" -Destination "C:/CI_Out_Report/" -Force
      PSEOF
    - |
      cat << PSEOF > /tmp/run_actt_container.ps1
      docker --config ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker run -d \`
        --name ${CI_JOB_ID} \`
        --network=${DOCKER_NETWORK} \`
        --env-file ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/ci.env \`
        -v ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report:C:/CI_Out_Report \`
        -v ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/${DUT_ACTT_CONFIG_DEST}:C:/app/test/environment/dut \`
        ${ACTT_IMAGE} powershell -Command 'Start-Sleep 3600'
      if (\$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Error 'Failed to start container'; exit 1 }
      docker network connect ${DOCKER_NETWORK2} ${CI_JOB_ID}
      docker exec ${CI_JOB_ID} powershell -File C:\CI_Out_Report\run_test.ps1
      \$exitCode = \$LASTEXITCODE
      docker stop ${CI_JOB_ID} | Out-Null
      docker rm ${CI_JOB_ID} | Out-Null
      exit \$exitCode
      PSEOF
    # Copy env file, test script, and Docker auth config to Windows host
    - scp /tmp/ci.env /tmp/run_test.ps1 /tmp/run_actt_container.ps1 ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/
    - scp -r /tmp/.docker ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker
    # DEBUG: verify Docker config (cmd has no `cat`; do not print full config.json — contains registry auth / job token material)
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker' -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Format-Table Name,Length -AutoSize\""
    # Pull ACTT image on Windows host using per-job Docker config (isolated credentials, safe for concurrent pipelines)
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "docker --config ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/.docker pull ${ACTT_IMAGE}"
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_actt_container.ps1
    # Remove helper files before pulling report to avoid leaking CI variables into artifacts
    - ssh ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST} "powershell -Command Remove-Item -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/ci.env','${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_test.ps1' ,'${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report/run_actt_container.ps1' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue"
    # Pull report back from Windows host to runner workspace
    - scp -r ${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}:${WIN_WORK_DIR}/report ./report
  after_script:
    # after_script runs in a new shell; ssh-agent is gone, use -i to specify key file directly
    - ssh -i "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY" -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}" "powershell -NoProfile -Command Remove-Item -Path '${WIN_WORK_DIR}' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue" || true
    - ssh -i "$ACTT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY" -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "${ACTT_SSH_USERNAME}@${ACTT_WINDOWS_HOST}" "docker image prune -f" || true
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - report/

.actt_upload_report:
  image: registry.gitlab.com/moxa/sw/sre/share/runner-img/docker-scm:latest
  variables:
    # Inherited from product autobuild_config.yml (pipeline variables); must not duplicate DUT_MODEL here or it overrides the product.
    # scm upload: --scm-path = SCM repo path; third arg = destination under repo → .../${DUT_MODEL}/report/${TEST_DATE}/
    ACTT_MAF_TARGET: "moxa/sw/sre/share/team-docker-images/maf/docker-actt"
  before_script:
    # Skip when the upstream actt job produced no report (e.g. it was skipped).
    - |
      if [ ! -d "report" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A report 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No ACTT report found, skip report upload.${LOG_END}"
        exit 3
      fi
  script:
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -z "${DUT_MODEL}" ] || [ "${DUT_MODEL}" = "NO_DEFAULT_DUT_MODEL" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: DUT_MODEL required for report upload path. Set it under variables: in autobuild_config.yml."
        exit 1
      fi
      if [ -n "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ] && [ -s "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" ]; then
        _SCM=$(sed -n 's/^SCM_URL=//p' "$FWR_PIPELINE_INFO_FILE" | head -n 1)
        _SCM=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed 's#/\([[:space:]]*\)#/#g')
        export DUT_SERIES=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed -n 's#.*[Ff][Ww][Rr]_\([^_]*\)_v.*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
        _VER=$(echo "$_SCM" | sed -n 's#.*/[Ff][Ww][Rr]_[^_]*_v\([^_]*\).*#\1#p' | head -n 1)
        export DUT_VERSION="$_VER"
        echo "actt_upload_report: DUT_MODEL=${DUT_MODEL} DUT_VERSION=${DUT_VERSION} DUT_SERIES=${DUT_SERIES}"
      fi
    - |
      set -e
      if [ -f report/result_summary.json ]; then
        TEST_DATE=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('report/result_summary.json'))['date'])")
      else
        echo "WARN: report/result_summary.json missing; using CI_PIPELINE_CREATED_AT for SCM path segment"
        TEST_DATE=$(date -d "$CI_PIPELINE_CREATED_AT" +"%Y-%m-%d-%H")
      fi
      echo "TEST_DATE=${TEST_DATE}"
      echo "Upload report/ → ${ACTT_MAF_TARGET}/${DUT_MODEL}/report/${TEST_DATE}/"
      scm upload --local-path report/ --scm-path "${ACTT_MAF_TARGET}" "report/${DUT_MODEL}/${TEST_DATE}"

aiTitle: GitLab CI pipeline測試結果輸出方式

content.text:
看完 `ci-pipeline` 的現況了，回答分兩層：一般設計、以及你們專案目前的落差。

## 一般設計：是 artifact，但通常是三層並用

GitLab 對「測試結果」其實有三個不同用途的機制，正式的 pipeline 通常同時用：

**1. `artifacts:paths` — 檔案下載（你問的那個）**
```yaml
artifacts:
  paths:
    - report/
  when: always          # ← 測試失敗才最需要報告
  expire_in: 30 days
  name: "$CI_PROJECT_NAME-$CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG-$CI_JOB_ID"
```
使用者從 job 頁面 Browse / Download，或用固定連結：
`https://<gitlab>/<group>/<proj>/-/jobs/artifacts/<branch>/download?job=<job-name>`（永遠指向該分支最後一次成功的 job，適合放在 wiki 給人抓）。

**2. `artifacts:reports:junit` — 結構化測試結果**
```yaml
artifacts:
  reports:
    junit: report/junit.xml
```
這個不是拿來下載的，是讓 GitLab 解析後顯示在 **Pipeline → Tests 分頁**和 **MR widget**：哪幾個 case fail、失敗訊息、跟上一次比較新增了哪些失敗。pytest 只要多加 `--junitxml=report/junit.xml` 就有，成本極低，但可讀性提升最大。

**3. 外部報告伺服器 — 長期保存 / 給沒有 GitLab 帳號的人看**
Artifact 有三個硬限制：有 expire、有大小上限（你們 build log 已經踩過，所以才改存 artifact）、而且**下載需要 GitLab 登入權限**。所以 HTML 報告、歷史趨勢一般丟到 Pages 或檔案伺服器。你們已經在做：`scm upload` 到 SCM，加上 Allure server。

實務上的分工大致是：**Tests 分頁看 pass/fail → artifact 抓當次 raw log 除錯 → 外部 server 看歷史趨勢與對外分享**。

## 你們專案目前的狀況

ACTT 那條線基本上已經是標準做法（artifact + SCM + Allure），但有兩個實際的漏洞：

**`.actt` 的 artifacts 缺 `when: always`**（`pipeline_main/actt.yml:172`）
```yaml
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - report/
```
GitLab 預設是 `when: on_success`。所以**測試真的失敗（exit 1）時，report/ 不會被上傳** — 而且 `auto-test:actt_upload_report` 用 `needs: artifacts: true` 取這份 artifact，拿不到就走 `exit 3` 跳過上傳。結果是：測試通過時報告齊全，測試失敗時報告全部消失，剛好跟需求相反。建議補 `when: always` 和 `expire_in`。

**BVT 完全沒有產出任何可下載的東西**（`pipeline_main/bvt.yml`）
目前只是 `ssh ... run_bvt.sh` 然後看 exit code，測試 log 留在 testbed 上。使用者要查失敗原因只能讀 job console output。若 `run_bvt.sh` 有產生 log/報告，建議在 script 尾端 `scp` 回 runner workspace 再宣告成 artifact，做法跟 ACTT 一樣。

要我動手補這兩個地方嗎？第一個是三行的事，第二個要先確認 `run_bvt.sh` 在 testbed 上把結果寫到哪個路徑。

===== upload_artifact.yml =====
.func_gen_scm_tag: &func_gen_scm_tag
  - |
    function gen_scm_tag() {
      IMG_FILE_NAME=$(ls upload | grep -E '^(FWR|MP).+\.rom$' | sed 's/\.[^.]*$//')
      if [ "${CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE}" != "schedule" ]; then
        PIPELINE_REASON=$(echo ${GITLAB_USER_NAME} | sed 's/ /_/g')
      fi
      if [[ ! -z "${BUILD_VER_MANUAL}" ]]; then
        BUILD_VER=$CI_PROJECT_NAME-$BUILD_VER_MANUAL
      fi
      SCM_TAG=${BUILD_VER}/${IMG_FILE_NAME}__${PIPELINE_REASON}
    }

    gen_scm_tag

.func_gen_pipeline_info: &func_gen_pipeline_info
  - |
    function gen_pipeline_info_file() {
      echo "Triggered_By=${GITLAB_USER_EMAIL}" > $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "CI_PIPELINE_ID=${CI_PIPELINE_ID}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "PRODUCT_CONFIG=${PRODUCT_CONFIG}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "MOXA_REV=${GIT_MOXA_REV}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "BUILDROOT_REV=${GIT_BUILDROOT_REV}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "GITLAB_BUILD_DOCKER_VER=${GITLAB_BUILD_DOCKER_VER}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "BUILD_VER"=${BUILD_VER} >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "BUILD_VER_MANUAL"=${BUILD_VER_MANUAL} >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE=${CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "FWR_FORCE_BUILD=${FWR_FORCE_BUILD}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      if [ -n "${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" ]; then
        echo "CI_COMMIT_TAG=${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
        echo "CI_COMMIT_TAG_MESSAGE=${CI_COMMIT_TAG_MESSAGE}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      fi
      echo "SCM_URL=${SCM_URL}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "BLACKDUCK_SCAN_CONFIG=${BLACKDUCK_SCAN_CONFIG}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG=${COVERITY_SCAN_CONFIG}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "RUST_CLIPPY_SCAN_CONFIG=${RUST_CLIPPY_SCAN_CONFIG}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "SQA_CI_TEST_LEVEL=${SQA_CI_TEST_LEVEL}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
      echo "SQA_CI_TESTBED_TYPE=${SQA_CI_TESTBED_TYPE}" >> $PIPELINE_INFO_FILE
    }

    SCM_URL="https://scm.moxa.com/${CI_PROJECT_PATH}/${SCM_TAG}.tar"
    echo -e "${LOG_INFO}}Upload build artifact to ${SCM_URL}${LOG_END}"
    gen_pipeline_info_file

.upload_artifacts:
  image: $SRE_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GITLAB_IMAGE_PREFIX/moxa/sw/sre/share/runner-img/docker-scm:latest
  variables:
    PIPELINE_INFO_FILE: "upload/PIPELINE_INFO.txt"
    PIPELINE_REASON: "daily"
    BUILD_VER: $CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG
  before_script:
    # Always publish a baseline config for next pipelines (per-branch), even when we skip upload.
    - |
      set -e
      mkdir -p baseline

      cfg=$(ls moxabuild/buildroot/output/images/FWR_*.config 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
      if [ -n "${cfg}" ]; then
        cp "${cfg}" baseline/FWR_baseline.config
      elif [ -f "${BASELINE_CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
        # No new build config produced; keep baseline available for the next pipeline.
        cp "${BASELINE_CONFIG_FILE}" baseline/FWR_baseline.config
      else
        echo "${LOG_INFO}No baseline config available to publish.${LOG_END}"
      fi

    # Early-exit to skip packaging/upload when there is no firmware output.
    - |

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Supported DUT models
SUPPORTED_MODELS=("rks-g4000-l3" "mds-g4000-l3" "tsn" "mds-g4000" "mds-g4000-l3-4xgs" "rks-g4000" "mds-g4000-4xgs" "tn-4500b" "eds-g4000" "65m-5011m" "mrx-q4000-l3" "rks-g4000-pl" "rks-g4000-pl-l3")

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <DUT_MODEL> <DUT_FWR_URL>"
    echo "Options:"
    echo "  -h, --help           Show this help and exit"
    echo "  --list-models        Print supported DUT models and exit"
}

list_models() {
    for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
        echo "$m"
    done
}

# Handle flags before positional args (safe with set -u)
case "${1-}" in
  --list-models)
    list_models
    exit 0
    ;;
  -h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

if [ -z "${1-}" ] || [ -z "${2-}" ]; then
    usage
    exit 1
fi

DUT_MODEL=$1
DUT_FWR_URL=$2

PWD=$(pwd)
DUT_MODEL_LOWER=$(echo "${DUT_MODEL}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
# Whitelist DUT models using array
is_supported=false
for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
        if [ "$m" = "${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}" ]; then
cp -f -- "${ROM_FILE_DIR}" "${TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR}"
ROM_FILENAME=$(basename "${ROM_FILE_DIR}")
echo "[TESTBED] copied rom file: ${ROM_FILENAME}"

### Start BVT Test ###
echo "[TESTBED] starting container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
docker start "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null

# Wait for bvt-container-network watcher to attach veth pairs (eth120/eth127).
# `docker start` returns before the watcher's async setup completes, so poll.
echo "[TESTBED] waiting for eth120/eth127 attach"
ATTACH_TIMEOUT=30
for i in $(seq 1 ${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}); do
    if docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth127 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth120 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
fi

# Execute the pytest command inside the Docker container
echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation, upgrade DUT to ${ROM_FILENAME}"
SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE="topology/topology_switch_rd_bvt_${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}.yaml"
SYNERGY_RD_BVT_FWR_UPGRADE="testcase/test_firmware_upgrade.py::TestFirmwareUpgrade::test_firmware_upgrade_rd_bvt_single_dut"
SYNERGY_RD_BVT_TEST_SUITE="rd_bvt"

PREP_CMD="cd switch_synergyautomation"
PREP_CMD="$PREP_CMD && sed -i \"s/firmware_version:.*/firmware_version: ${ROM_FILENAME}/\" ${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"
PREP_CMD="$PREP_CMD && python -m pytest ${SYNERGY_RD_BVT_FWR_UPGRADE} --allure-no-capture --topology_config_path=${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"

docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$PREP_CMD"
BVT_PREP_RESULT=$?
if [ ${BVT_PREP_RESULT} -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation failed (ret=${BVT_PREP_RESULT})"
    docker stop "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null
    exit ${BVT_PREP_RESULT}
fi
echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation completed (ret=${BVT_PREP_RESULT})"

echo "[TESTBED] executing BVT tests in container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
TEST_CMD="cd switch_synergyautomation"
TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD && python -m pytest -m ${SYNERGY_RD_BVT_TEST_SUITE} --allure-no-capture --topology_config_path=${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"


docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$TEST_CMD"
BVT_RESULT=$?
echo "[TESTBED] BVT execution completed (ret=${BVT_RESULT})"

echo "[TESTBED] stopped container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
docker stop "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null

exit ${BVT_RESULT}

BVT testbed PC (`switch-rd-testbed`, user `switch_rd_testbed`) hosts multi-DUT containers sharing the same management IP 192.168.127.20 via per-VLAN isolation. Veth+bridge design validated end-to-end on 2026-04-22 (RKS/MDS ping to DUT and NPort confirmed working).

**Why:** Each DUT has fixed management IP 192.168.127.253; containers need the same IP (192.168.127.20) so automation code stays identical across DUTs. VLAN isolates the /24 subnet per-DUT.

**How to apply:** When adding a new model or debugging the testbed, consult this layout first.

## Systemd watcher

`bvt-container-network.service` runs `bvt_container_network_watcher.sh`, which listens to `docker events --filter event=start` and re-runs `setup_bvt_container_network.sh <model>` on every container start (boot, `docker start`, `docker restart`). Host VLAN/bridge persists via `/etc/network/interfaces.d/`; only veth + in-namespace IPs need re-attach.

## Backup containers

`synergy_switch_rks-g4000-l3_bvt_macvlan` — the original RKS container (Docker macvlan on `vlan10_net`, IP 192.168.127.129) renamed as backup before the veth rebuild. To roll back RKS: stop veth version, rename macvlan back to original name, `docker start`.

## Container run flags gotcha

Must use `docker run -dit` (not just `-d`). The image's entrypoint `tftp_configure.sh` `exec`s to `bash`; without a tty, bash hits EOF immediately, `--restart always` restart-loops. Confirmed via log "使用提供的 CONTAINER_IP ... 正在配置 TFTP 服務器" repeating endlessly.

aiTitle: GitLab CI pipeline測試結果輸出方式

content.text:
三個問題都能做，但有兩個前置的坑必須先解掉，否則「失敗時也要有 report」這條做不到。

## 2) 格式建議 — `artifacts:reports:junit` 是對的，而且看得到

**看得到。** GitLab 解析 junit.xml 後會顯示在：
- **Pipeline → Tests 分頁**：每個 test case 一列，PASS / FAIL / SKIP、耗時、失敗的 traceback，還會標出「這次新增的失敗」
- MR widget 的測試摘要區塊

這正好對應你的需求 1（各測項 PASS/FAILED 反映在 report 上），而且你們 BVT 本來就是 `python -m pytest`，只要加 `--junitxml=report/junit.xml` 就有，零成本。

一個容易踩的點：`reports:junit:` 宣告的檔案在 UI 上**不保證可瀏覽/下載**（依 GitLab 版本而異）。標準做法是同一個檔案在兩處都列：

```yaml
artifacts:
  when: always
  expire_in: 30 days
  paths:
    - report/                    # ← 給使用者下載
  reports:
    junit: report/junit.xml      # ← 給 GitLab 解析成 Tests 分頁
```

建議 `report/` 內容分三種用途：

| 檔案 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `junit.xml` | GitLab Tests 分頁、機器可讀 |
| `bvt_run.log` | pytest 完整 console output，除錯用 |
| `allure-results/` | 人看的報告。你們 ACTT 已經有 Allure server（`10.123.25.160`），BVT 的 pytest 也已經掛了 allure plugin（`--allure-no-capture`），加 `--alluredir` 就能產出 |
| `result_summary.json` | 總數/pass/fail/日期，給 SCM 路徑命名與後續 dashboard 用（ACTT 已有同名慣例） |

不建議自己刻 HTML 報告 — junit + Allure 已經覆蓋「機器讀」和「人讀」兩種需求。

## 0) SCM 上傳位置

`upload_artifact.yml:41` 的 SCM 路徑組成是：
```
https://scm.moxa.com/${CI_PROJECT_PATH}/${BUILD_VER}/${IMG_FILE_NAME}__${PIPELINE_REASON}.tar
```
BVT stage 已經會從 `PIPELINE_INFO.txt` 解析 `SCM_URL`，所以能直接推出同一層目錄，放成韌體 `.tar` 的兄弟檔：
```
.../${BUILD_VER}/${IMG_FILE_NAME}__${PIPELINE_REASON}_BVT_REPORT.tar
```
（已經打包好的韌體 tar 沒辦法事後塞東西進去，所以只能是同目錄的另一個檔案。）

**但有個執行面限制**：`scm` CLI 在 `docker-scm` image 裡，而 BVT job 跑在 RDVM runner 上用預設 image、沒有 `scm`。ACTT 就是為此拆成 `auto-test:actt` + `auto-test:actt_upload_report` 兩個 job。BVT 要照抄這個模式：`bvt`（RDVM，跑測試、產 report artifact）→ `bvt_upload_report`（docker-scm image，`needs: artifacts: true` 接手上傳）。

## 1) 成功/失敗都要有 report — 這裡有兩個 blocker

**Blocker A：`run_bvt.sh` 的 `set -e` 讓失敗路徑是死碼**

`BVT_PC/run_bvt.sh:1` 是 `set -euo pipefail`，而 178-180 行：
```bash
docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$PREP_CMD"
BVT_PREP_RESULT=$?
if [ ${BVT_PREP_RESULT} -ne 0 ]; then ...
```
`docker exec` 一旦非 0，`set -e` 當場中止腳本，`BVT_PREP_RESULT=$?` 和底下的 if 根本不會執行 — 連 `docker stop` 清理都跳過了。192-193 行的 `TEST_CMD` 同樣。**測試失敗時腳本直接死掉，任何收報告的程式碼都不會跑到**，所以需求 1 在現況下必然失敗。要改成：
```bash
docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$TEST_CMD" || BVT_RESULT=$?
```

**Blocker B：prep 階段（韌體升級）失敗時完全沒有測項結果**

`test_firmware_upgrade.py` 那一跑也是 pytest，同樣加 `--junitxml` 就能產出一份「升級失敗」的 junit，不會變成一片空白的報告。建議 prep 和 test 各產一份（`junit_prep.xml` / `junit.xml`），或用不同 `-o junit_suite_name` 合併。

另外，報告檔案要落在 host 看得到的地方。`switch_synergyautomation` 是從 `/home/switch_rd_testbed/switch_synergyautomation/` bind mount 進容器的，所以寫在該目錄下 host 直接就有，不需要 `docker cp` — 但那是**所有 model 共用**的目錄，建議寫到 per-run 的子目錄（用 `CI_JOB_ID` 或 model+timestamp）避免不同 model 併發時互相覆蓋。

---

## 我要動的檔案

1. `BVT_PC/run_bvt.sh` — 修 `set -e` 失敗路徑、pytest 加 `--junitxml` / `--alluredir`、報告輸出到 per-run 目錄、產 `result_summary.json`
2. `ci-pipeline/pipeline_main/bvt.yml` — `scp -r` 把報告拉回 runner workspace、宣告 `artifacts` (`when: always` + `paths` + `reports:junit`)
3. `ci-pipeline/switch_ci_pipeline.yml` — 新增 `bvt:upload_report` job（docker-scm image，`needs` 接 bvt artifact，`scm upload` 到韌體 tar 同目錄）

開工前有兩件我無法自己確認的事：

**a. `run_bvt.sh` 怎麼部署到 testbed？** pipeline 是 `ssh ... "bash ./run_bvt.sh"`，跑的是 testbed 家目錄那份；repo 裡 `BVT_PC/` 下有 `run_bvt.sh`、`.orig`、`.change`、`brainstorm/run_bvt.sh` 好幾份。我該改哪一份、之後是手動 scp 過去還是有同步機制？

**b. SCM 用 `_BVT_REPORT.tar` 這個兄弟檔命名可以嗎？** 還是你希望放到 `${BUILD_VER}/bvt_report/` 之類的子目錄？

這兩點確認後我就直接實作。

1	#!/bin/bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	# Supported DUT models
5	SUPPORTED_MODELS=("rks-g4000-l3" "mds-g4000-l3" "tsn" "mds-g4000" "mds-g4000-l3-4xgs" "rks-g4000" "mds-g4000-4xgs" "tn-4500b" "eds-g4000" "65m-5011m" "mrx-q4000-l3" "rks-g4000-pl" "rks-g4000-pl-l3")
6	
7	usage() {
8	    echo "Usage: $0 <DUT_MODEL> <DUT_FWR_URL>"
9	    echo "Options:"
10	    echo "  -h, --help           Show this help and exit"
11	    echo "  --list-models        Print supported DUT models and exit"
12	}
13	
14	list_models() {
15	    for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
16	        echo "$m"
17	    done
18	}
19	
20	# Handle flags before positional args (safe with set -u)
21	case "${1-}" in
22	  --list-models)
23	    list_models
24	    exit 0
25	    ;;
26	  -h|--help)
27	    usage
28	    exit 0
29	    ;;
30	esac
31	
32	if [ -z "${1-}" ] || [ -z "${2-}" ]; then
33	    usage
34	    exit 1
35	fi
36	
37	DUT_MODEL=$1
38	DUT_FWR_URL=$2
39	
40	PWD=$(pwd)
41	DUT_MODEL_LOWER=$(echo "${DUT_MODEL}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
42	# Whitelist DUT models using array
43	is_supported=false
44	for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
45	        if [ "$m" = "${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}" ]; then
46	                is_supported=true
47	                break
48	        fi
49	done
50	if [ "$is_supported" != true ]; then
51	        echo "[TESTBED] unsupported DUT model: ${DUT_MODEL}"
52	        echo "[TESTBED] supported models: ${SUPPORTED_MODELS[*]}"
53	        exit 1
54	fi
55	DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME="synergy_switch_${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}_bvt"
56	TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR="${PWD}/download/${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
57	TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR="${PWD}/material/${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
58	FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME=$(basename "${DUT_FWR_URL}" | sed 's/\.[^.]*$//')
59	
60	### BVT Preparation ###
61	# Download the firmware artifact from the provided URL
62	if [ ! -d "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted" ]; then
63	    echo "[TESTBED] downloading firmware from ${DUT_FWR_URL}"
64	    mkdir -p "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}"
65	    wget -P "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}" "${DUT_FWR_URL}"
66	
67	    # Extract the .tar file
68	    echo "[TESTBED] extracting ${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}"
69	    mkdir -p "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted"
70	    tar -xf "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar" -C "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted"
71	    rm -f "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar"
72	else
73	    echo "[TESTBED] firmware already downloaded: ${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar"
74	fi
75	
76	# Copy downloaded files to the material directory.
77	# Prefer FWR*.rom (device firmware). Some packages (e.g. MRX) also ship BOOT_*.rom
78	# (bootloader); a plain *.rom find can pick BOOT first and fail device-firmware upgrade.
79	echo "[TESTBED] Copy rom file to material directory"
80	ROM_FILE_DIR=$(find "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted" -type f -name 'FWR*.rom' -print -quit)
81	if [ -z "${ROM_FILE_DIR}" ]; then
82	    echo "[TESTBED] no FWR*.rom found in the extracted contents"
83	    exit 1
84	fi
85	mkdir -p "${TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR}"
86	cp -f -- "${ROM_FILE_DIR}" "${TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR}"
87	ROM_FILENAME=$(basename "${ROM_FILE_DIR}")
88	echo "[TESTBED] copied rom file: ${ROM_FILENAME}"
89	
90	### Start BVT Test ###
91	echo "[TESTBED] starting container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
92	docker start "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null
93	
94	# Wait for bvt-container-network watcher to attach veth pairs (eth120/eth127).
95	# `docker start` returns before the watcher's async setup completes, so poll.
96	echo "[TESTBED] waiting for eth120/eth127 attach"
97	ATTACH_TIMEOUT=30
98	for i in $(seq 1 ${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}); do
99	    if docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth127 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
100	       && docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth120 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
101	        echo "[TESTBED] interfaces ready after ${i}s"
102	        break
103	    fi
104	    if [ "$i" -eq "${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}" ]; then
105	        echo "[TESTBED] ERROR: eth120/eth127 not attached within ${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}s"
106	        echo "[TESTBED] check 'sudo systemctl status bvt-container-network.service'"
107	        exit 1
108	    fi
109	    sleep 1
110	done
111

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Supported DUT models
SUPPORTED_MODELS=("rks-g4000-l3" "mds-g4000-l3" "tsn" "mds-g4000" "mds-g4000-l3-4xgs" "rks-g4000" "mds-g4000-4xgs" "tn-4500b" "eds-g4000" "65m-5011m" "mrx-q4000-l3" "rks-g4000-pl" "rks-g4000-pl-l3")

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <DUT_MODEL> <DUT_FWR_URL>"
    echo "Options:"
    echo "  -h, --help           Show this help and exit"
    echo "  --list-models        Print supported DUT models and exit"
}

list_models() {
    for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
        echo "$m"
    done
}

# Handle flags before positional args (safe with set -u)
case "${1-}" in
  --list-models)
    list_models
    exit 0
    ;;
  -h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

if [ -z "${1-}" ] || [ -z "${2-}" ]; then
    usage
    exit 1
fi

DUT_MODEL=$1
DUT_FWR_URL=$2

PWD=$(pwd)
DUT_MODEL_LOWER=$(echo "${DUT_MODEL}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
# Whitelist DUT models using array
is_supported=false
for m in "${SUPPORTED_MODELS[@]}"; do
        if [ "$m" = "${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}" ]; then
                is_supported=true
                break
        fi
done
if [ "$is_supported" != true ]; then
        echo "[TESTBED] unsupported DUT model: ${DUT_MODEL}"
        echo "[TESTBED] supported models: ${SUPPORTED_MODELS[*]}"
        exit 1
fi
DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME="synergy_switch_${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}_bvt"
TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR="${PWD}/download/${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR="${PWD}/material/${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME=$(basename "${DUT_FWR_URL}" | sed 's/\.[^.]*$//')

### BVT Preparation ###
# Download the firmware artifact from the provided URL
if [ ! -d "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted" ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] downloading firmware from ${DUT_FWR_URL}"
    mkdir -p "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}"
    wget -P "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}" "${DUT_FWR_URL}"

    # Extract the .tar file
    echo "[TESTBED] extracting ${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}"
    mkdir -p "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted"
    tar -xf "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar" -C "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted"
    rm -f "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar"
else
    echo "[TESTBED] firmware already downloaded: ${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}.tar"
fi

# Copy downloaded files to the material directory.
# Prefer FWR*.rom (device firmware). Some packages (e.g. MRX) also ship BOOT_*.rom
# (bootloader); a plain *.rom find can pick BOOT first and fail device-firmware upgrade.
echo "[TESTBED] Copy rom file to material directory"
ROM_FILE_DIR=$(find "${TESTBED_DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FWR_ARTIFACT_NAME}_extracted" -type f -name 'FWR*.rom' -print -quit)
if [ -z "${ROM_FILE_DIR}" ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] no FWR*.rom found in the extracted contents"
    exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "${TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR}"
cp -f -- "${ROM_FILE_DIR}" "${TESTBED_MATERIAL_DIR}"
ROM_FILENAME=$(basename "${ROM_FILE_DIR}")
echo "[TESTBED] copied rom file: ${ROM_FILENAME}"

### Start BVT Test ###
echo "[TESTBED] starting container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
docker start "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null

# Wait for bvt-container-network watcher to attach veth pairs (eth120/eth127).
# `docker start` returns before the watcher's async setup completes, so poll.
echo "[TESTBED] waiting for eth120/eth127 attach"
ATTACH_TIMEOUT=30
for i in $(seq 1 ${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}); do
    if docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth127 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" ip link show eth120 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "[TESTBED] interfaces ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if [ "$i" -eq "${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}" ]; then
        echo "[TESTBED] ERROR: eth120/eth127 not attached within ${ATTACH_TIMEOUT}s"
        echo "[TESTBED] check 'sudo systemctl status bvt-container-network.service'"
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

# Ensure DUT route exists (safety net for veth-based network setup)
echo "[TESTBED] verifying container network routes"
docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c \
    "ip route show 192.168.127.0/24 | grep -q eth127 || ip route add 192.168.127.0/24 dev eth127 2>/dev/null || true"
docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "ip addr"
docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "ip route"

# Verify DUT reachability.
# Retry to tolerate transient packet loss (e.g. LAN switch saturated while
# other testbeds upgrade concurrently): probe every 5s, give up after 3 min.
echo "[TESTBED] verifying network connectivity to DUT"
PING_RETRY_INTERVAL=5
PING_RETRY_TIMEOUT=180
ping_deadline=$((SECONDS + PING_RETRY_TIMEOUT))
dut_reachable=false
while :; do
    if docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c \
        "ping -c 2 -W 3 -I eth127 192.168.127.253" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        dut_reachable=true
        break
    fi
    if [ "${SECONDS}" -ge "${ping_deadline}" ]; then
        break
    fi
    echo "[TESTBED] DUT not reachable yet, retrying in ${PING_RETRY_INTERVAL}s"
    sleep "${PING_RETRY_INTERVAL}"
done
if [ "${dut_reachable}" != true ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] ERROR: cannot reach DUT at 192.168.127.253 within ${PING_RETRY_TIMEOUT}s"
    exit 1
fi
echo "[TESTBED] DUT reachable"

# Verify NPort connectivity with the same retry policy (every 5s, up to 3 min).
# NPort failure is non-fatal, so on timeout we only warn instead of exiting.
echo "[TESTBED] verifying NPort connectivity"
nport_deadline=$((SECONDS + PING_RETRY_TIMEOUT))
nport_reachable=false
while :; do
    if docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c \
        "ping -c 2 -W 3 -I eth120 192.168.120.254" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        nport_reachable=true
        break
    fi
    if [ "${SECONDS}" -ge "${nport_deadline}" ]; then
        break
    fi
    echo "[TESTBED] NPort not reachable yet, retrying in ${PING_RETRY_INTERVAL}s"
    sleep "${PING_RETRY_INTERVAL}"
done
if [ "${nport_reachable}" != true ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] WARNING: cannot reach NPort at 192.168.120.254 within ${PING_RETRY_TIMEOUT}s"
else
    echo "[TESTBED] NPort reachable"
fi

# Execute the pytest command inside the Docker container
echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation, upgrade DUT to ${ROM_FILENAME}"
SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE="topology/topology_switch_rd_bvt_${DUT_MODEL_LOWER}.yaml"
SYNERGY_RD_BVT_FWR_UPGRADE="testcase/test_firmware_upgrade.py::TestFirmwareUpgrade::test_firmware_upgrade_rd_bvt_single_dut"
SYNERGY_RD_BVT_TEST_SUITE="rd_bvt"

PREP_CMD="cd switch_synergyautomation"
PREP_CMD="$PREP_CMD && sed -i \"s/firmware_version:.*/firmware_version: ${ROM_FILENAME}/\" ${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"
PREP_CMD="$PREP_CMD && python -m pytest ${SYNERGY_RD_BVT_FWR_UPGRADE} --allure-no-capture --topology_config_path=${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"

docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$PREP_CMD"
BVT_PREP_RESULT=$?
if [ ${BVT_PREP_RESULT} -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation failed (ret=${BVT_PREP_RESULT})"
    docker stop "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null
    exit ${BVT_PREP_RESULT}
fi
echo "[TESTBED] BVT preparation completed (ret=${BVT_PREP_RESULT})"

echo "[TESTBED] executing BVT tests in container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
TEST_CMD="cd switch_synergyautomation"
TEST_CMD="$TEST_CMD && python -m pytest -m ${SYNERGY_RD_BVT_TEST_SUITE} --allure-no-capture --topology_config_path=${SYNERGY_TOPOLOGY_FILE}"


docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" bash -c "$TEST_CMD"
BVT_RESULT=$?
echo "[TESTBED] BVT execution completed (ret=${BVT_RESULT})"

echo "[TESTBED] stopped container ${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}"
docker stop "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>&1 >/dev/null

exit ${BVT_RESULT}
